The goal is to leverage proven ideas from modern app packaging (like AppImage, APK, Electron’s ASAR, game engines) and innovate beyond them to make .tear fast, secure, modular, tier-aware, and user-friendly. Comparison of Container Formats and Their Attributes To inform the .tear design, it’s useful to examine how existing app containers and package formats work. The table below highlights popular formats, focusing on their structure, launch process/speed, and modularity/self-containment traits: Format Structure & Packaging Launch & Execution Modularity / Self- Containment .exe (Windows EXE) Portable Executable (PE) binary; may embed resources (icons, UI layouts, etc.) but code and data are compiled into a single file . Often accompanied by separate .dll files for libraries. Double-click to load by OS loader. Very fast startup (binary is executed directly by CPU). Requires correct OS/CPU architecture and any required DLLs present. If using .NET or JVM, needs runtime installed. Not inherently modular (the .exe is fixed once compiled). Contains a structured Contents directory with subfolders: MacOS/ for the Mach-O executable, Resources/ for assets (icons, media, nibs), Info.plist manifest for metadata, and code signatures . Treated as an application by Finder. Double-click opens the main binary in Contents/MacOS . Launch is quick, though first launch may trigger Gatekeeper checks (verifying the _CodeSignature to ensure no tampering ). After that, the app runs natively at full speed. Highly self-contained (all resources and frameworks can be inside the .app ). Can include plugins or frameworks in Contents/Plugins or Contents/ Frameworks . Modularity via bundle extensions (e.g. app can load optional plugins from its bundle). Updating usually means replacing the whole bundle (difficult to modify parts without breaking signature). .apk (Android Package) A ZIP-based archive (JAR format) . Standard structure: AndroidManifest.xml (app metadata and permissions) , classes.dex (compiled Dalvik bytecode) , res/ (resources indexed by resources.arsc ), assets/ (developer-defined files like HTML, media, etc.) , lib/ (compiled native libraries for various CPU ABIs) , and META-INF/ (signing certificates and checksums for integrity) . All files are compressed inside the APK. Must be installed via the Android OS. Installation unpacks the APK, verifies signatures, and compiles the bytecode to native (ART) or caches it.
